correctness.rationale: The literal closed-neighborhood NOR rule is exactly \(F(S)=E([n]\setminus U(S))\), whose support cases give \(F^3=F\) and the complete orbit/first-entry classification for every \(n\ge4\). Counting exact supports by inclusion-exclusion proves all basin formulas. An explicit injection gives \(c_n>2c_{n-2}\), hence unique basin dominance. Bonferroni pair intersections for two isolated base vertices give the exact sharp asymptotic after correcting for the empty initial graph. Two different code implementations exhaustively verify \(n=4,5,6\) and \(n=4,5,6,7\), respectively; the proof covers every \(n\ge4\).

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the full individual attraction-basin census and sharp dominant-basin asymptotic for self-inclusive NOR on the triangular graphs L(K_n), n>=4. The universal period-two restriction and broadly general periodic-point counts are acknowledged known; in particular the 2020 (N-2)-regular corollary covers only the T_4 periodic-point count and not any basin size. The available full primary texts do not imply the exact individual triangular-graph basin counts nor the rare-two-isolated-vertices asymptotic without a new explicit structural reduction and count. The inaccessible 2012 maxterm/minterm paper and unindexed work remain real overlap risks.
residual_risks: The 2012 maxterm/minterm orbital paper was available only as abstract/metadata; a full-text comparison could reveal a stronger formula.
A specialized L(K_n) NOR attraction-basin calculation could exist under a different terminology or in an unindexed source.
The general 2020 neighborhood-image formula covers some periodic-point counts; this claim does not treat that component as the substantive novelty.

value.rationale: The canonical triangular graph family L(K_n) provides a natural controlled test of self-inhibitory graph dynamics. Individual attraction-basin sizes and asymptotic measure concentration are intrinsic, motivated robustness invariants. The sharp asymptotic separates exponentially many recurrent orbits from one basin with asymptotically all initial states; the theorem fully classifies this family rather than choosing an ad hoc finite case or claiming a general known periodicity fact.
